charter.mission: Implement the approved bug-reporter revision 12 end to end in Artemis: synchronously freeze bounded diagnostic context, collect reporter intent and managed images in the Quickfile composer, prepare one trusted RenderedReport on the server, and deliver that value either to Jira or as a streamed ZIP bundle while preserving the existing Artemis debugger.
conventions: Keep the three-value pipeline explicit: CapturedContext, BugContextEnvelope, then immutable RenderedReport.
Concentrate trusted derivation, allowlisting, budgets, image validation, and rendering in prepareBugReport; do not fragment that boundary into pass-through classes.
Use Atlantis components and existing Artemis UI primitives for the composer; preserve semantic class conventions and avoid arbitrary design tokens.
Use registered validation through cctl validate; never invoke the registered Jest, ESLint, TypeScript, formatter, or pre-merge scripts directly.

Design budgets are fixed for this delivery: 6 images including capture, 5 MB per image, 20 MB aggregate images, 24 MiB total request, 140-character image descriptions, 4,000-character observed/expected/reproduction fields, 8,192 px per axis, 40 MP, 32 KiB per provider, 128 KiB total providers, 64 KiB flags, 512 KiB context, and a shared 64 KiB 15-minute telemetry digest capped at 20 errors and 30 failed requests.

Quickfile is a 440 px anchored one-screen card; the 860 ms capture beat is non-blocking motion over an already-frozen value and is skipped for prefers-reduced-motion. The unknown-outcome recovery state may exceed the normal footprint.
nonGoals: Production or GovCloud enablement, redaction or screenshot masking, a captured-context ledger, durable delivery, an outbox, retries after ambiguous Jira creation, OAuth 2LO, rate limiting, report history, Jira workflow management, and autonomous fixes are out of scope.
Do not add a second provider registry, a local file sink, server-side report persistence, a browser-to-Jira path, or a runtime sink selector.
Do not remove the debug log buffer, the artemis-debugger MCP server, its three tools, or temporary debug-only registration.

Operational governance is outside this delivery: agents do not provision or govern Jira accounts, assign attachment ACL or retention ownership, manage credential expiry or rotation, certify deployed permissions, own Datadog retention, obtain ingress-owner approval, or track cross-team notifications.
vocabulary: CapturedContext: immutable synchronous browser snapshot taken before the composer renders.
RenderedReport: immutable Jira issue fields plus ordered attachment bytes consumed by Jira and ZIP delivery.
Unknown outcome: a single ambiguous Jira create attempt whose draft and reportId are retained and which offers search plus bundle recovery but no resend.
charter.testStrategy: Use red-green-refactor TDD for behavior. Before implementation, add a behavior-level test that fails on the missing behavior, then run only that single test file with `cctl validate run test --wait -- <test-file>`; scaffold only enough module shape to avoid import/setup failures. Keep focused tests green during refactoring. The final verification context runs the registered pre-merge gate and drives the real feature through this worktree's dev server. Pure documentation, configuration wiring, and visual-only styling may skip test-first when the task summary states why.
knownAmbiguities: The active session charter contained older privacy assumptions. The user explicitly decided on 2026-08-22 that approved revision 12 governs: lower environments contain no real customer data, captured content is not redacted or masked, the panel does not disclose context, and Download bundle replaces the local sink.

R18 authorizes the combined V3/V4 migration. The implementation keeps the V3 diff minimal and names the touched files in its handoff; tracking map-team notification is operational governance and does not block this delivery.
The historical Quickfile prototype does not draw the unknown-outcome state; revision 12 and this plan charter define the required state and override that omission.

invariants.statement: Approved revision 12 and this plan charter govern; their no-redaction, no-masking, streamed-bundle, and no-panel-disclosure decisions supersede conflicting older session text.
Behavior changes follow red-green-refactor with a failing behavior-level test run through the registered single-file test command before implementation.

Integration evidence exercises authenticated production composition paths with controlled external seams; availability or governance of externally provisioned Jira credentials does not block implementation verification.
Enablement is explicit and defaults off; Dev alone is true, GovCloud is refused in code and config, and neither NODE_ENV nor APP_ENVIRONMENT alone controls the feature.

One always-live provider registry serves bounded report projections and development-only verbose projections while the debugger bridge, log buffer, MCP tools, and low-ceremony debug registration remain functional.
Changes under the V3-sensitive map paths are limited to the registration-call migration and projection, preserve the import fence, and include no formatting, cleanup, or unrelated refactor.

Capture paths never read credentials, cookies, storage contents, authorization headers, raw cache rows, request or response bodies, console history, or serialized DOM; query parameter values are the intentional exception.
Identity, tenant, deployment, commit, reporter attribution, and timestamps are derived or verified on the server and have no accepted client-authored representation.
Jira and Download bundle consume the same immutable RenderedReport; environment does not select a sink and report artifacts are never persisted server-side.

Jira traffic and credentials remain server-only, CSP continues to exclude atlassian.net, and HTTP Basic with the dedicated service-account email and API token is the sole delivered authentication path.
A timeout, connection loss, or 5xx after Jira creation starts produces one create attempt and an unknown outcome; the UI retains the draft and offers search plus bundle recovery without resend.

executionContexts.title: Build the unified context registry
executionContexts.description: Introduce the canonical always-live registry and split debug serialization, bridge, and log buffering into focused modules without migrating production registrations yet.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Report-provider IDs are author-declared and stable across unregister/re-register, with duplicate handling that throws in development and records a deployed warning without mount-order suffixes.

registerReportProvider requires the report schema, schemaVersion, byte budget, timeout, collect projection, and optional collectVerbose; registerDebugProvider accepts only an id and collector and is structurally ticket-ineligible.
Throwing, over-time, and over-budget providers yield scoped warnings while unrelated providers remain present independent of registration order, and collected values are cloned at freeze time.
A dual-projection provider sends collect output to report capture and collectVerbose output to the development bridge; a collect-only provider supplies the bounded projection to both consumers.
The separate debug log buffer retains the 5,000-entry bound, overflow count, destructive drain, run-id gating, and error-swallowing behavior required by the MCP poller.

executionContexts.title: Land shared contracts, budgets, and gating
executionContexts.description: Create the canonical schemas and configuration surfaces consumed by browser, server, provider, and route branches before those branches implement against them.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Checked-in Zod contracts define submission, timing receipt, bug-context.json, flags.json, RenderedReport inputs, results, and provider projections, with a schemaVersion-coupled golden round trip.
Route helpers retain template, resolved path, and query values and resolve a parameterized route template to its page module for a fixture-backed machine consumer.

ENABLE_BUG_REPORTER defaults false, resolves true only for Dev, resolves explicit false for production and both GovCloud blocks after YAML merge keys, and is wired through public/server schemas and deployment config.
One enablement module makes GovCloud an unconditional false and exposes client-render and server-enforcement callers without consulting NODE_ENV or APP_ENVIRONMENT alone.
The shared flags contract and helper reconstruct a sorted non-default delta plus declared relevant flags against flag-defaults.json and trusted commit SHA.
The log sanitizer names Jira credential and receipt-secret keys explicitly, and serialization tests prove seeded values are removed.

executionContexts.title: Migrate both map providers
executionContexts.description: Apply the authorized V3/V4 registration migration with one shared schema and tree-local projections while preserving the map isolation fence and a reviewable minimal diff.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The active V3 or V4 map registers semantic id map and projects zoom, center, basemap, visible layers, selected entity, active panel, and filter summary without data rows.
The registration is present in both map-state providers and either implementation validates against the same tree-neutral provider schema without cross-map imports.
Tracked changes under V3-sensitive map paths are limited to imports, registration-call replacement, projection construction, and behavior tests; the import-fence rule is unchanged.
The implementation handoff names the V3-sensitive files and keeps the change portable; tracking or obtaining map-team notification is outside the implementation workflow.

The company profile report projection contains entity, active tab/sub-tab, expanded sections, and per-section loaded-versus-pending state.
Recognizable query rows, response payloads, and whole-store sentinels seeded in tests do not appear in either provider projection.

executionContexts.title: Cut over registrations and preserve debugger tooling
executionContexts.description: Migrate the remaining query-cache and rel-builder registrations, expose the compatible development bridge, delete the old registry surface, and update debugger documentation and MCP coverage.

queryCache and relBuilderStore use the unified APIs, both map sites arrive from map-provider-migration, and no source import or export of src/lib/debug/debug-registry.ts remains.
The old debug registry module is removed after its serialization, log-buffer, and bridge responsibilities have canonical replacement homes, leaving one provider registry.
artemis_list_providers, artemis_snapshot, and artemis_logs return equivalent provider, snapshot, and drain behavior through the real MCP bridge.
window.__artemisDebug and a verbose sentinel are absent from a production bundle while bounded report collection remains active in production-built lower environments.
The debugger skill, instrumentation reference, and MCP README teach the two unified registration APIs and contain no removed-registry import example.

executionContexts.title: Implement trusted report preparation
executionContexts.description: Build receipt verification, server-owned derivation, allowlist validation, budgets, image validation, and deterministic envelope assembly behind prepareBugReport.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Freeze and screenshot phases issue short-lived signed receipts, submission verifies them and stamps submittedAt, and delayed-submission tests show three distinct server-sourced timestamps.

An outer stripping schema accepts a body containing spoofed trusted keys, yet prepareBugReport derives identity, tenant, deployment, commit, reporter ID, and timing exclusively from authenticated server inputs.
Only known provider id/schemaVersion pairs with schema-valid bounded data enter the envelope; unknown, mismatched, debug-only, or invalid projections become capture warnings.
Server preparation enforces field, provider, envelope, image-count, per-image, aggregate-image, attachment, decompressed, request, signature, dimension, and pixel limits with typed refusals.

PNG/JPEG bytes are detected and decoded under bounds, forwarded unchanged after validation, and assigned deterministic non-colliding names that distinguish automatic capture from reporter-added images.

Structural and seeded-sentinel tests show preparation and capture contracts contain no credentials, storage, headers, raw rows, bodies, console history, or serialized DOM and introduce no reporter-content scrubber.

executionContexts.title: Render Jira content and stream the bundle
executionContexts.description: Produce the immutable RenderedReport, ADF and report.md representations, ordered attachments, and an in-memory/streamed ZIP from one preparation result.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: RenderedReport contains distinct bug-context.json and flags.json attachments, and bug-context.json carries no evaluated flag values.
Summary, observed, expected, reproduction text, and image descriptions enter ADF solely through typed text constructors and match an exact adversarial-character fixture.
Attachment order is bug-context.json, flags.json, then retained images in reporter order, with image descriptions beside filenames and in matching envelope entries.
The ZIP contains bug-context.json, flags.json, report.md, and retained images under server names, and its issue model plus attachment bytes equal the Jira consumer's RenderedReport input.
Bundle generation returns a bounded stream or in-memory body with a deterministic archive name and performs no filesystem, database, repository, or temporary-file report write.

executionContexts.title: Implement Jira delivery and outcome semantics
executionContexts.description: Create the fetch-backed injected Jira client, server-only credential boundary, issue mappings, attachment upload, and no-duplicate outcome state machine against RenderedReport. External account provisioning and governance are inputs, not workflow gates.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The default client uses fetch with one server-only HTTP Basic credential provider, exposes no OAuth/auth-mode switch, leaves CSP without atlassian.net connect access, and excludes credential material from public config and logs.

TRACK and VOGUE alone are accepted, with server-held component IDs, Bug type, Bugs category, mapped severity, fixed labels, unset sprint/fix version, and environment-consistent summary/envelope labels.
Issue creator and native reporter remain the service account while the Artemis Reporter ID field receives only the server-derived opaque reporter identifier.

An injected fake asserts create and attachment method, URL, Basic header presence, ADF body, multipart part name file, X-Atlassian-Token no-check, ordering, error mapping, and credential-header caching.
Timeout, connection loss, and 5xx produce one create request and unknown outcome; only provable pre-send failures and a definite 429 honoring Retry-After may retry.
An attachment failure returns the created key plus failed filename/status, writes a missing-attachment note to that issue, does not retry the file, and does not create another issue.
No created outcome exists without a Jira key, attachment work begins only after creation confirms, and repeated submission of one guarded request invokes create once.
A test substitutes another credential provider without changing capture, preparation, rendering, bundling, route composition, or Jira request semantics.

Credentials are read from server environment only, committed config carries no value, local and deployed paths share gates and limits, and locally-created issues remain visibly distinct from Dev issues.

The implementation consumes server-only service-account email/token configuration and documents required Jira operations, but does not provision accounts, inspect expiry, certify deployed grants, manage rotation, or assign attachment ACL/retention ownership.

executionContexts.title: Compose the authenticated bug-report route
executionContexts.description: Wire freeze, screenshot, submit-to-Jira, and Download bundle phases through one authenticated App Router handler and expose the server-derived capability used by the client.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The production route returns 401 before identity, 404 when disabled or GovCloud, enforces origin/content type/request bounds, and rechecks enablement on each phase.
Missing or invalid Jira configuration makes canCreateIssue false and the creation action return alertable 503 while the bundle action remains functional.
Authenticated identities from two organizations reach preparation without role, permission, connection, cohort, or identity-allowlist checks.

The multipart submit path invokes prepareBugReport once, dispatches its RenderedReport to Jira or ZIP delivery by requested action, and maps typed preparation/delivery results to the specified HTTP outcomes.
Freeze and screenshot receipt phases run through the same authenticated route, GovCloud refusal, enablement rule, and error mapping as submission without duplicating a second endpoint.

executionContexts.title: Freeze browser context and images
executionContexts.description: Implement synchronous browser capture, telemetry, route/flags/Datadog context, lazy screenshot capture, image normalization, and receipt advancement as a never-throwing client boundary.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The trigger guard mints reportId, freezes provider/route/flags/Datadog/telemetry state synchronously, and records invocation order before React renders the composer.
A throwing provider, elapsed-time violation, and rejected screenshot become scoped capture warnings while the frozen report remains submittable.
Captured context includes template, resolved path, query values, reconstructable flag inputs, and Datadog application/session/view IDs plus UTC window and same-reportId markers without a replay link.

Listeners capture bounded/deduplicated uncaught errors and unhandled rejections; application interceptors add failed-request method, query-stripped path, status, duration, and owned trace ID while successes, cancellations, console calls, and bodies remain absent.
html2canvas is lazily imported, excludes reporter UI, reports blank-canvas/iframe degradation, honors reduced motion, and records failed status without blocking composer availability.
Automatic, pasted, and selected images are decoded/re-encoded to the supported formats so the preview Blob and submitted Blob are the same object with the original filename discarded.

executionContexts.title: Build the Quickfile composer
executionContexts.description: Mount the Dev-only reporter root at the application shell, render the one-screen Atlantis composer, manage intent and images, and preserve the reported page and draft.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Opening and closing the portal-mounted reporter leaves a mount-counting page probe unchanged and does not navigate, replace keys, or wrap the reported page conditionally.
Observed and expected text alone block submission when empty; each not-sure choice writes explicit ticket text, reproduction stays optional, and severity defaults Low without blocking.
Image detail shows readable pixels, server-intended filename, origin, bytes, description, Replace, and Remove without masks, annotation tools, masking claims, or redaction affordances.
Paste/select can add or replace images, remove can leave zero images, count/per-image/aggregate/description limits refuse at add time with named limits, and drag/order changes remain deterministic.

The composer DOM exposes only signal count, snapshot timestamp, route, capture-state dot, environment badge, and image previews; seeded identity, permissions, flags, RUM, telemetry, and provider data remain absent.
Reporter-authored draft fields and image metadata are retained in memory plus sessionStorage for reload recovery without creating a browsable report history or treating storage as captured context.

executionContexts.title: Wire submit, bundle, and recovery states
executionContexts.description: Connect the frozen draft and Quickfile UI to the production route with identical multipart bodies and honest created, partial, failed, and unknown outcome behavior.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The server-derived capability offers Create Jira ticket plus Download bundle when ready and Download bundle alone when Jira is unconfigured, independent of local versus deployed environment.
Send and Download bundle build byte-equivalent multipart submissions from the same frozen draft and differ only by requested terminal action.
Definitive failure, partial success, and unknown outcome retain observed/expected/reproduction/project/severity, images, descriptions, order, and the original reportId.
Unknown outcome shows the original reportId, manual Jira search link, and Download bundle, offers no resend or copy-as-text action, and preserves the guarded one-create-call behavior.
Created UI appears only with a key; upload progress begins after the key, partial success names missing files and waits for input, and the trigger retains a copyable key for the session.
One-click bundle download names the ZIP, byte size, and contained files, states that Jira was not contacted, and exposes report.md as the human-readable recovery artifact.

executionContexts.title: Verify the composed feature end to end
executionContexts.description: Inspect the integrated tree, repair bounded gaps, run the full registered gate, and drive the real app, bundle, debugger, and Jira composition paths without making external governance a delivery gate.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A bounded audit confirms the Dev/GovCloud matrix, one registry, removed legacy imports, CSP exclusion, Basic-only server auth, excluded-class source fence, and absence of report persistence or masking code.

Through this worktree's cctl-provided dev URL, an authenticated browser freezes before paint, keeps the reported page mounted, manages intent/images, and reaches bundle-only or Jira-ready actions from server capability.

A downloaded ZIP is opened and its schema-valid JSON, report.md, image names/order/hashes, trusted environment/timestamps, provider projections, and excluded-data sentinels are verified against the filed draft.

Production route composition and the injected Jira transport prove allowed-project mappings, opaque reporter attribution, fixed environment labeling, ADF, and JSON/image multipart uploads. A live marked issue may be created when credentials are already configured, but external credential availability or governance does not block delivery.
The artemis-debugger MCP lists migrated providers, snapshots bounded/verbose projections through the development bridge, and drains the preserved log buffer on a mounted application page.

The registered pre-merge command passes on the integrated tree after focused regression tests cover identity spoofing, provider isolation, ambiguous creation, bundle equivalence, and panel non-disclosure.

conventions: Keep the three-value pipeline explicit: CapturedContext, BugContextEnvelope, then immutable RenderedReport.
Concentrate trusted derivation, allowlisting, budgets, image validation, and rendering in prepareBugReport; do not fragment that boundary into pass-through classes.
Use Atlantis components and existing Artemis UI primitives for the composer; preserve semantic class conventions and avoid arbitrary design tokens.
Use registered validation through cctl validate; never invoke the registered Jest, ESLint, TypeScript, formatter, or pre-merge scripts directly.

Design budgets are fixed for this delivery: 6 images including capture, 5 MB per image, 20 MB aggregate images, 24 MiB total request, 140-character image descriptions, 4,000-character observed/expected/reproduction fields, 8,192 px per axis, 40 MP, 32 KiB per provider, 128 KiB total providers, 64 KiB flags, 512 KiB context, and a shared 64 KiB 15-minute telemetry digest capped at 20 errors and 30 failed requests.

Quickfile is a 440 px anchored one-screen card; the 860 ms capture beat is non-blocking motion over an already-frozen value and is skipped for prefers-reduced-motion. The unknown-outcome recovery state may exceed the normal footprint.
nonGoals: Production or GovCloud enablement, redaction or screenshot masking, a captured-context ledger, durable delivery, an outbox, retries after ambiguous Jira creation, OAuth 2LO, rate limiting, report history, Jira workflow management, and autonomous fixes are out of scope.
Do not add a second provider registry, a local file sink, server-side report persistence, a browser-to-Jira path, or a runtime sink selector.
Do not remove the debug log buffer, the artemis-debugger MCP server, its three tools, or temporary debug-only registration.

Operational governance is outside this delivery: agents do not provision or govern Jira accounts, assign attachment ACL or retention ownership, manage credential expiry or rotation, certify deployed permissions, own Datadog retention, obtain ingress-owner approval, or track cross-team notifications.
vocabulary: CapturedContext: immutable synchronous browser snapshot taken before the composer renders.
RenderedReport: immutable Jira issue fields plus ordered attachment bytes consumed by Jira and ZIP delivery.
Unknown outcome: a single ambiguous Jira create attempt whose draft and reportId are retained and which offers search plus bundle recovery but no resend.
